subject: Sapphire pilot — request for temporary SLO adjustments & commercial offset
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@sapphireai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLO ask — high-throughput trial next month

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — the team was impressed with the inference latency and the quantization roadmap. We're ramping a time-limited pilot (production traffic patterns, not just a toy workload) and need to confirm whether Redwood can temporarily relax two SLOs for the pilot window so we can validate throughput and cost benefits: 

- Uptime SLO: allow 99.5% for the pilot period (90 days) vs your standard 99.9%.
- Latency SLO: p95 target of 400ms for the pilot (our current expected p95 with our bursty traffic); we understand 250ms is your default.

We are prepared to accept stricter remediation triggers and added observability (extra tracing hooks) during the pilot. Commercially, Sapphire is asking for a 25% pilot discount on committed GPU-hours as an offset for the non-standard SLOs — we can commit to a 6-month pilot volume if we get temporary SLO relief for the first 90 days.

Attached is our traffic sample and a short note from our infra team about expected burst windows. Can you confirm whether this is something we can do, and what approvals you need?

Appreciate it — Claire

--
Claire Huang
Head of Platform, Sapphire AI
claire@sapphireai.com
+1 (415) 555-0172
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — high-throughput trial next month

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding the ask from Sapphire. Quick summary: they want a temporary relaxation for uptime to 99.5% and a higher latency p95 during a 90-day pilot. They're offering a 25% pilot discount contingent on the SLO carve. They also propose extra tracing and we have their traffic sample attached.

Questions for deal desk / ops:
- Is a temporary 99.5% uptime carve permissible for a pilot that will be production-like?
- What service-credit cap do we want if we grant this? (they asked for commercial offset — pricing can be our lever)
- Any legal/contract redlines on a time-limited SLO amendment (Kim)?

I think a conditional approval that ties the relaxation to a strict monitoring/rollback plan & a hard credit cap is reasonable. If we want to keep the credit small, we should offer 2 months of 50% off (or equivalent) rather than a wholesale 25% ongoing discount.

Attaching their files. Jonas — can you run a quick ops feasibility check?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask — high-throughput trial next month

On Sun, Jul 18, 2027 at 12:04 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa / Jonas — forwarding the ask from Sapphire. Quick summary: they want a temporary relaxation for uptime to 99.5% and a higher latency p95 during a 90-day pilot.

I reviewed their traffic sample (pilot_traffic_metrics.csv). Tech assessment: their burst profile will stress leader election and cold-starts in our multi-tenant pool at the scale they propose. We can support a temporary SLO variance, but only with these guardrails: 

1) Dedicated pool reservation for the pilot (to reduce cross-tenant impact). Requires revenue commitment (3 months minimum).
2) Active KV-prefix caching enabled + mandatory prefix warming window in each deploy.
3) Monitoring & automatic rollback: if availability dips below 99.2% for any 24h window, we auto-failover them to a pinned regional pool and unwind the pilot.

Commercial recommendation: approve the SLO relaxation for 90 days if we get a capped remedy: max service-credit exposure = 30% of the monthly pilot invoice in any billing cycle. Offer a commercial offset: 2 months at 40% discount (applied as credit) instead of an up-front 25% continuous discount. That keeps our downside bounded while giving them predictable runway.

I'll prepare an ops note for Legal with the required rollback hooks.

- Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting exec sign-off: Sapphire pilot SLO variance (DEAL-5871)

Folks —

This is a recommendation to grant a conditional 90-day SLO variance for Sapphire's pilot with the following commercial and operational controls: 

- SLO adjustments: uptime target set to 99.5% for the pilot window; latency p95 tolerance to 400ms.
- Operational guardrails: dedicated capacity, prefix-warming, auto-rollback if 24h availability < 99.2%.
- Commercials: 2 months at 40% discount (credited toward pilot usage) in lieu of an open-ended 25% discount; service-credit cap of 30% of monthly pilot invoice.

This preserves product trust (we require dedicated capacity + rollback) and limits our credit exposure. If Legal (Kim) signs off on the contract amendment language, I'd like exec approval to proceed so Karthik can close and get a DocuSign sent.

Lauren — can you confirm approval or flag concerns? Goal: communicate final terms to Sapphire by EOD and stand up the dedicated pool before the pilot start date.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

I approve the conditional 90-day SLO variance per your terms. Two clarifying points before we send to the customer: 
1) Legal needs a short exhibit that explicitly states the rollback trigger and the operational steps (we should avoid vague language on automated rollback). Kim, please prepare that amendment and I'll sign.
2) Finance to confirm the credit accounting treatment for the 2-month 40% credit (Jonas, please loop finance). We should book the committed usage revenue up front and apply the credit to invoices — finance ops will advise.

Once Legal and Finance confirm, Karthik: send the DocuSign with exhibit and explicit pilot start/end dates. Notify infra to reserve a dedicated pool with the agreed resource floor.

Good work — approve to proceed.

Lauren
